vendors.name: AutoCount
vendors.tagline: Malaysian accounting, POS, HRMS and cloud accounting with LHDN e-Invoice
vendors.market_position: AutoCount is developed by Auto Count Sdn Bhd of Petaling Jaya, a wholly owned subsidiary of Autocount Dotcom Berhad, which moved from the ACE Market to the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia on 26 February 2026. It sells the on-premise Accounting 2.0 in five editions plus Cloud Accounting, POS and HRMS. AutoCount says over 240,000 companies use its accounting software and that it has 300+ dealers.
pros: On-premise and cloud editions
Direct LHDN MyInvois submission through its own e-Invoice Platform
Cloud plans include standard, consolidated and self-billed e-invoices
Dealer and training-centre network (300+ of each, per AutoCount)
cons: No public prices for the desktop Accounting 2.0 editions
SST, project and multi-currency are plug-ins on desktop editions
Annual cloud discount is a limited-time promotion
General accounting, not a construction-specific product
vendors.typical_pricing: Cloud Accounting: Lite RM70/month (1 user plus 1 accountant), Basic RM100, Plus RM140, Pro RM180 per month; 12-month plans list at RM840-RM2,160 per year, with a limited-time 60% discount shown. Prices exclude SST. Desktop Accounting 2.0: no public prices; sold through dealers.
vendors.my_specific_note: AutoCount says its AutoCount e-Invoice Platform (AIP) connects directly to LHDN MyInvois for standard, consolidated and self-billed e-invoices, and queues and retries submissions while MyInvois is down. Auto Count Sdn Bhd is also a Peppol certified access point under MDEC. Its Cloud Accounting plans include e-Invoice at no extra cost; on the desktop editions SST is an optional plug-in.

vendors.name: SQL Account
vendors.tagline: Malaysian accounting and payroll software, desktop or cloud, with LHDN e-Invoice
vendors.market_position: SQL Account is developed by E Stream MSC Sdn Bhd, founded in 2003, with offices in Shah Alam and Kuala Lumpur. It runs on the desktop, on SQL Cloud or on a private cloud, alongside SQL Payroll, SQL HRMS and other add-on products. E Stream says more than 320,000 companies use SQL and that it has over 1,000 business partners.
pros: Published cloud prices from RM79 per month
E-invoice, consolidated and self-billed e-invoices to LHDN MyInvois
Desktop, public cloud or private cloud deployment
Support centres across Malaysia, including Sabah and Sarawak
cons: No public prices for desktop licences
Additional cloud users cost RM60 per month each
SST treatment of the listed prices not stated
General accounting, not a construction-specific product
vendors.typical_pricing: SQL Account Cloud: Essential RM79/month, Pro RM109/month, plus RM60/month per additional user. SQL Payroll Cloud from RM69/month per company (up to 20 staff). E Stream's pricing page does not say whether SST is included. Desktop licences: no public prices; sold through partners.
vendors.my_specific_note: E Stream says SQL Account submits e-invoices to LHDN MyInvois in one click, supports consolidated and self-billed e-invoices, and can generate a QR code so customers enter their own details for an e-invoice. E Stream MSC Sdn Bhd is a Peppol certified access point under MDEC, and its site says SQL Account covers SST.

vendors.name: Financio (by ABSS)
vendors.tagline: Cloud accounting and payroll for Malaysian SMEs from ABSS
vendors.market_position: Financio is the cloud accounting and payroll product of Asian Business Software Solutions (ABSS), the former MYOB South Asia, which rebranded to ABSS in 2018 and launched Financio in Malaysia and Singapore in 2017. The Star reported in June 2022 that Censof Holdings had raised its stake in ABSS to 97%. ABSS also sells the desktop ABSS Accounting and Premier range and says more than 400,000 SMEs use its software.
pros: Published prices from RM50 per month
LHDN e-invoices included in both plans
Payroll product from the same vendor
30-day free trial of the Premier plan
cons: Essentials plan includes only 25 LHDN e-invoices
No permanently free plan
SST treatment of the listed prices not stated
No construction job-costing features found on its pages
vendors.typical_pricing: Accounting Essentials RM50/month or RM550/year; Accounting Premier RM85/month or RM935/year (prices effective 1 December 2024). Payroll Essentials RM75/month (up to 30 employees), Payroll Premier RM135/month (up to 200 employees). SST treatment not stated. 30-day free trial; no free plan.
vendors.my_specific_note: Financio says its users can send, receive and track e-invoices with LHDN, and its e-invoice guide covers consolidated and self-billed e-invoices and credit or debit notes. The Essentials plan includes 25 LHDN e-invoices and Premier 5,000, so check the quota against your invoice volume.

vendors.name: Bukku
vendors.tagline: Malaysian cloud accounting with a free invoicing plan and LHDN e-Invoice
vendors.market_position: Bukku is a cloud accounting product from Nukleus Ventures Sdn Bhd, with a free invoicing plan for new companies and four paid accounting plans, all with unlimited users. Nukleus Ventures is a Peppol certified access point under MDEC, Malaysia's Peppol authority. Bukku says 65,000+ companies have activated its software.
pros: Free Launch invoicing plan for new companies and startups
Published prices from RM35 per month, with unlimited users
Peppol certified access point (MDEC)
Standard, consolidated and self-billed e-invoices to MyInvois
cons: Paid plans are charged 8% SST on top of the listed price
SST and multi-currency are add-ons on the Seed and Grow plans
Launch plan is aimed at companies under six months old
No construction job-costing features found on its pages
vendors.typical_pricing: Launch: free (invoicing, for new companies and startups). Seed RM35/month or RM350/year; Grow RM65/month or RM650/year; Prime RM95/month or RM950/year; Elite RM135/month or RM1,350/year; all paid plans plus 8% SST, unlimited users.
vendors.my_specific_note: Bukku says e-invoice submission to LHDN MyInvois is one click from its invoices and that it handles consolidated and self-billed e-invoices, on every plan including the free one. Its developer, Nukleus Ventures Sdn Bhd, is on the Peppol list of certified access points under MDEC.

vendors.name: Biztory Cloud Accounting
vendors.tagline: Malaysian cloud accounting and invoicing with LHDN e-invoice submission
vendors.market_position: Biztory is a cloud accounting product from Biztory Cloud Sdn Bhd (formerly Vectory Innovation Sdn Bhd) of Puchong, Selangor, founded in 2014. It covers sales, purchases, inventory, accounting and e-invoicing, with project management on its Pro plan. Biztory's about page says it serves more than 6,500 businesses in Malaysia.
pros: Published yearly prices from RM690
E-invoice submission included on every plan
Consolidated and self-billed e-invoice submission
Project management on the Pro plan
cons: Plans are billed yearly
Plus plan has no full-set accounting or SST features
SST treatment of the listed prices not stated
Elite plan (unlimited users) is quote-only
vendors.typical_pricing: Billed yearly: Plus RM690/year (2 users), Growth RM1,290/year (10 users), Pro RM2,490/year (30 users); Elite custom priced. SST treatment not stated. 14-day free trial.
vendors.my_specific_note: Biztory says it submits e-invoices to LHDN automatically, including self-billed invoices, and lets users consolidate receipts and submit them together instead of keying each into the MyInvois portal. Full-set accounting and SST features start on the Growth plan.

vendors.name: Access UBS (formerly Sage UBS)
vendors.tagline: UBS accounting, billing, inventory and payroll, now Access UBS Evo
vendors.market_position: UBS, formerly sold as Sage UBS, is now marketed in Malaysia as Access UBS Evo by The Access Group, which bought Sage's Australia and Asia business in 2021. Access Group Malaysia, based at Exchange 106 in Kuala Lumpur, sells UBS accounting, billing, inventory, POS, building service maintenance and UBS Payroll modules. Sage's own Malaysian site could not be read, so Sage 300 and X3 are not covered here.
pros: Accounting, billing, inventory, POS and payroll modules
Generates SST-02 and SST-02A forms
Classification-code mapping for LHDN e-invoicing
Local Access Group office in Kuala Lumpur
cons: No public prices
Name change from Sage UBS to Access UBS can confuse buyers
E-invoice submission method not stated on its pages
No construction job-costing module named on its UBS pages
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices on The Access Group's UBS pages.
vendors.my_specific_note: The Access Group says UBS Evo generates SST-02, SST-02A and Laporan CJ(P) Jadual C-01 forms and maps product classification codes for the LHDN e-invoice mandate, with e-invoices sent and received from within UBS. Existing Sage UBS users should check which UBS version they need for e-invoicing.

vendors.name: HashMicro
vendors.tagline: Modular ERP with a construction module, sold in Malaysia by HashMicro Malaysia
vendors.market_position: HashMicro sells a modular ERP covering accounting, HR and payroll, inventory, CRM, procurement, manufacturing, POS, project management and construction. Its Malaysian site is run by HashMicro Malaysia Sdn Bhd from Wisma UOA II in Kuala Lumpur, and it lists offices in Singapore, Indonesia, the Philippines, Australia and Thailand. HashMicro says 3,000+ companies use its software.
pros: Construction module with BoQ templates and progress billing
Subcontractor work orders and claims
HashMicro says its e-invoicing is integrated with MyInvois
Broad module range in one ERP
cons: No public prices
Its own ERP comparison article lists HashMicro first; treat such lists as marketing
Full ERP scope is more than many small contractors need
Certification claims in its e-invoice guide not backed by an official list
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices on HashMicro's Malaysian site.
vendors.my_specific_note: HashMicro says its e-invoice software is integrated with LHDN MyInvois for automatic validation and submission. Its construction module covers BoQ templates, milestone progress billing with retention and subcontractor claims. Its Malaysian blog ranks HashMicro first in its own ERP list, so compare it against independent sources.

vendors.name: BuildSpace (BuildSpace Pro)
vendors.tagline: Malaysian cloud platform for construction tendering, estimating and project delivery
vendors.market_position: BuildSpace is made by Global PCK Solutions Sdn Bhd of Kuala Lumpur, which cites research dating back to 2011. Its eProject platform covers project cost preparation, tender submission and on-site progress evaluation for developers, main contractors, subcontractors and consultants, alongside the BuildSpace Pro estimating tool and the ProcureX procurement platform. Its site shows clients including Gamuda, PKNS and YTL Construction.
pros: Built for Malaysian developers, contractors and consultants
Covers cost preparation, tendering and progress evaluation
Estimating tool with built-in quantity surveyor procedures
Procurement platform (ProcureX) for suppliers and materials
cons: No public prices: demo request only
Construction-only: no general accounting
No e-invoicing features described; needs separate accounting software
Aimed at project teams more than small trade firms
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. BuildSpace offers a free demo on request.
vendors.my_specific_note: BuildSpace is a Kuala Lumpur product used on Malaysian projects by developers and contractors such as Gamuda, PKNS and YTL Construction, according to its site. It covers tendering, estimating and progress evaluation, not LHDN e-invoicing, so pair it with accounting software for MyInvois submission.

vendors.name: Cubicost by Glodon
vendors.tagline: BIM quantity takeoff and cost estimating (Cubicost TAS, TRB, TME, TBQ)
vendors.market_position: Cubicost is the 5D BIM cost-estimating suite of Glodon Company Limited, founded in China in 1998 and listed on the A-share market since 2010 (stock code 002410). Its Asia site lists a Malaysia office at Jaya One, Petaling Jaya, and case studies from Malaysian firms including WT Partnership and Sunline M&E. The suite includes TAS for quantity takeoff, TRB for rebar takeoff, and TME and TBQ.
pros: BIM quantity takeoff with built-in local measurement rules
3D rebar takeoff (TRB) with auto-deduction
Works with Revit BIM models
Malaysia office in Petaling Jaya and Malaysian case studies
cons: No public prices: demo request only
Estimating and takeoff only: no accounting or e-invoicing
Separate products per trade (TAS, TRB, TME, TBQ)
Aimed at quantity surveyors and estimators, not small trade firms
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices on Glodon's Asia site. Glodon offers demos on request.
vendors.my_specific_note: Glodon's Asia site lists a Malaysia office in Petaling Jaya (+603 7931 6081) and Malaysian case studies from QS and M&E firms. Cubicost is a takeoff and estimating tool, not an LHDN MyInvois tool, so it pairs with accounting software for e-invoicing.

vendors.name: RIB CostX
vendors.tagline: 2D and BIM takeoff with estimating spreadsheets live-linked to drawings
vendors.market_position: RIB CostX, first sold as Exactal CostX, is a takeoff, estimating and reporting product from RIB Software, which says it is part of Schneider Electric. It measures from 2D drawings, PDFs and 3D BIM models into live-linked estimating workbooks, and comes in Complete, Core and Quantify packages. RIB lists APAC offices in Australia, China, India and New Zealand but none in Malaysia.
pros: Takeoff from 2D drawings, PDFs and 3D BIM models
Estimating spreadsheets live-linked to drawings
Automatic revision handling
Standalone, network or cloud (CostX Cloud) licensing
cons: No public prices: custom quote only
No Malaysian office listed by RIB
Estimating only: no accounting or e-invoicing
Aimed at quantity surveyors and estimators, not small trade firms
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices. RIB gives custom prices for its Complete, Core and Quantify packages through a form on its site.
vendors.my_specific_note: RIB lists no Malaysian office, so Malaysian buyers get prices through RIB's global quote form. CostX is a takeoff and estimating layer only; it does no LHDN MyInvois or SST work, so pair it with local accounting software.

vendors.name: Globe3 ERP
vendors.tagline: ERP with construction project accounting, progress claims and an LHDN e-invoice module
vendors.market_position: Globe3 ERP comes from TNO Systems Pte Ltd of Singapore, which says the business started in 2002, and is sold in Malaysia by Globe3 Systems Sdn Bhd from Damansara Heights, Kuala Lumpur. It targets construction, trading, manufacturing, field service, equipment rental and other industries. Globe3's Singapore site says it serves 1,200+ businesses.
pros: Construction project costing, WIP accounting and progress claims
Subcontractor approval, backcharges and a sub-con e-submission portal
E-Invoice Malaysia module for LHDN submissions
Malaysian office in Kuala Lumpur
cons: No public prices
Full ERP scope is more than many small contractors need
E-invoice page does not detail consolidated or self-billed support
Developed by a Singapore company, sold locally by its Malaysian arm
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices on Globe3's Malaysian site.
vendors.my_specific_note: Globe3 says its E-Invoice Malaysia module automates LHDN-compliant submissions and that it offers integration services for e-invoicing. Its construction module covers project costing, construction WIP accounting, progress and certified claims and subcontractor backcharges, with local sales from Globe3 Systems Sdn Bhd in Kuala Lumpur.

vendors.name: IFCA MSC Berhad
vendors.tagline: Malaysian property and construction ERP vendor, listed on Bursa Malaysia
vendors.market_position: IFCA MSC Berhad is a Petaling Jaya-based software company, listed on Bursa Malaysia since July 2003 (stock code 0023). Its X-series suite includes ContractX for construction management, PropertyX for property developers, AccountX, HRX and an e-invoicing module. IFCA lists six offices in Malaysia plus offices in Singapore, China and Indonesia.
pros: ContractX covers progress claims, variation orders, retention, subcontracts and purchasing
IFCA says its ERP suite, including ContractX, submits e-invoices to LHDN by direct API
Listed company that publishes annual and quarterly reports
Offices in Petaling Jaya, Penang, Johor Bahru, Kuantan, Kuching and Kota Kinabalu
cons: No public prices: quote from IFCA only
Built for contractors running multiple projects; a large system for a sole trader
Construction, property, accounting and HR are separate products in the suite
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public prices.
vendors.my_specific_note: Malaysian-developed and headquartered in Petaling Jaya. IFCA says ContractX handles progress claims, certifications, retention and subcontractor purchase-on-behalf invoices, and that its ERP suite submits e-invoices to LHDN's MyInvois system through a direct API.

vendors.name: ePerolehan (Government eProcurement)
vendors.tagline: The Malaysian federal government's online procurement system for goods and services
vendors.market_position: ePerolehan is the Government of Malaysia's official online procurement system, launched in 2000 under the MSC Electronic Government initiative and developed under the purview of the Ministry of Finance. Commerce Dot Com, which the government appointed to develop and operate it, says it covers federal procurement of goods and services from supplier registration and quotation requests through to contracts and payment.
pros: Official federal government procurement system, developed under the Ministry of Finance
Quotations, purchasing, contract management and payment in one system, per its operator
Operator Commerce Dot Com runs service centres and a training portal for users
cons: Federal government procurement only, per its operator; other buyers advertise elsewhere
Suppliers must register before taking part; current fees not confirmed here
A procurement system, not a tender-alert service
vendors.typical_pricing: Not confirmed: check current supplier registration fees on the ePerolehan portal.
vendors.my_specific_note: Operated by Commerce Dot Com for the Government of Malaysia under an outsourcing model. Supplier registration, the registration guide and the supplier FAQ are on the ePerolehan portal; works contractors should also check each tender's CIDB grade requirements.

vendors.name: CIDB e-Tender & N3C
vendors.tagline: Tender notices from Malaysia's construction industry regulator, CIDB
vendors.market_position: The Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB) registers Malaysian contractors in grades G1 to G7. Its website posts tender notices among its announcements, such as rail station walkway and park-and-ride works notices in May 2026, and links to a separate e-Tender system at eiklan.cidb.gov.my. A further CIDB page lists overseas project opportunities under its international mission programme.
pros: Run by the construction industry's statutory registration body
Tender notices on CIDB's site are open to read without logging in
CIDB publishes its contractor registration fees for each grade
cons: The e-Tender site (eiklan.cidb.gov.my) did not load when checked on 30 September 2026
Notices are posted as images among general announcements, with little detail in text
Overseas listings page shows old entries, one closing in December 2019
Not a tender-alert or search service
vendors.typical_pricing: Tender notices free to read. CIDB contractor registration: RM20 (G1) to RM1,400 (G7), plus a RM50 processing fee for new registration or re-registration (RM30 for renewals), per CIDB.
vendors.my_specific_note: Contractors register and check their grade through CIDB's CIMS system. CIDB also says a levy of 0.125% applies to construction contracts worth more than RM500,000.

vendors.name: Tenderpanel
vendors.tagline: Malaysian government tender search and alerts, filtered by licence category
vendors.market_position: Tenderpanel is a Malaysian subscription service that collects tenders and quotations from government agencies into one searchable database, with daily email alerts matched to a user's keywords and licences. It says it covers CIDB, MOF/KKM, UPKJ and PUKONSA requirements and links each notice back to the original. The Pro plan adds past award records and a contractor directory.
pros: Prices for both plans published on its site
Daily email alerts matched to keywords and CIDB, MOF/KKM, UPKJ and PUKONSA licences
Each listing links back to the original government notice, per Tenderpanel
Pro plan shows past award winners, contract values and contract periods
cons: Covers government agency tenders; no private-sector coverage stated
No operating company named on its About or Terms pages
Its terms say it does not warrant the accuracy or completeness of its information
vendors.typical_pricing: Basic RM1,648 a year and Pro RM2,438 a year (RM137 and RM203 a month on that basis), per Tenderpanel's pricing page; tax not stated. Tenderpanel says yearly billing saves 31-32% against monthly billing.
vendors.my_specific_note: Built around Malaysian licence schemes: users filter by CIDB, MOF/KKM, UPKJ and PUKONSA registrations. Pro subscribers also get a public company page, which Tenderpanel says can bring inbound leads.

vendors.name: Recommend.my
vendors.tagline: Malaysian home-services marketplace where customers get quotes from vetted pros
vendors.market_position: Recommend.my is run by RecomN Technologies Sdn Bhd of Petaling Jaya, which says it started in 2014 and also runs Sejasa.com in Indonesia. Customers post a request and receive quotes (up to five for complex projects) or book fixed-price services, across categories such as renovation, electrical, aircon, cleaning and repairs. Its homepage cites 10,000 vendors and 200,000 customers served.
pros: Pros pay a lead fee only when a customer exchanges contact details, per Recommend.my
Vetting checks SSM registration, owner ID and, for renovation work, CIDB certification
Customers paying online get protection up to RM100,000, which can reassure buyers
Payouts for online-paid jobs in 1-2 business days
cons: Lead fee and commission rates are not published
Commission is charged on completed jobs on top of lead fees
Complex jobs go to up to five quoting pros, so price competition is direct
vendors.typical_pricing: No public prices for pros: a lead fee when a customer exchanges contact details, plus commission on completed jobs (rates not published). No customer fee stated.
vendors.my_specific_note: Renovation and interior design pros must show CIDB certification to join, per Recommend.my. Kaodim, another Malaysian home-services marketplace, shut down in June 2022.

vendors.name: Allianz General Malaysia
vendors.tagline: Contractors' All Risks cover from the Malaysian arm of the Allianz Group
vendors.market_position: Allianz General Insurance Company (Malaysia) Berhad is a wholly owned subsidiary of Allianz Malaysia Berhad, which is listed on Bursa Malaysia; the Allianz Group became the controlling shareholder in 2001. Its Contractors' All Risks policy covers damage to the contract works and third-party liability for the contract period. It is sold through agents and brokers or by contacting Allianz, which lists 30 branches nationwide.
pros: One policy covers material damage to the works and third-party liability
Optional cover for construction plant, machinery, debris removal, professional fees and the principal's existing property
Product Disclosure Sheets and proposal form downloadable in English and Malay
30 branches nationwide, per Allianz Malaysia
cons: No published premium rates; priced after a proposal form
No online purchase for CAR: through an agent, a broker or Allianz's contact form
Cover is written per contract, for the period in the Letter of Award
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no published premium rates.
vendors.my_specific_note: Allianz says its CAR cover runs for the contract period in the Letter of Award, with optional extensions for construction plant and equipment, machinery, debris removal, professional fees and the principal's existing property. Allianz Malaysia states it is a PIDM member.

vendors.name: Lonpac Insurance
vendors.tagline: General insurer in the LPI Capital group, with a Contractor's All Risks product
vendors.market_position: Lonpac Insurance is the general insurance subsidiary of LPI Capital Bhd, whose shares trade on Bursa Malaysia. In October 2024 Public Bank agreed to buy a 44.15% stake in LPI Capital from the late founder's family, and its follow-on general offer lapsed in January 2025 below the 50% acceptance level, per The Star and The Edge. Lonpac lists Contractor's All Risks among its engineering and machinery covers for businesses.
pros: Contractor's All Risks offered as a named business product
Parent LPI Capital is listed and reports its results publicly
Member of the General Insurance Association of Malaysia (PIAM)
Also writes business insurance in Singapore, through its own Singapore site
cons: No published premium rates; quote required
The CAR web page gives little readable detail; ask for the Product Disclosure Sheet
No online purchase route for CAR found
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no published premium rates.
vendors.my_specific_note: Contractor's All Risks sits under Lonpac's engineering and machinery covers for businesses. Ask a Lonpac agent or broker for the Product Disclosure Sheet and policy wording before comparing quotes.

vendors.name: MSIG Malaysia
vendors.tagline: Malaysian general insurer owned by Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance (MS&AD group)
vendors.market_position: MSIG Insurance (Malaysia) Bhd is a Kuala Lumpur-based general insurer licensed under the Financial Services Act 2013 and regulated by Bank Negara Malaysia. It describes itself as a subsidiary of Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance and part of Japan's MS&AD group, and says it writes fire, engineering and motor business. Its current website lists fire, marine, cyber and SME package cover for businesses, but no Contractors' All Risks page was found.
pros: Subsidiary of Mitsui Sumitomo Insurance, part of Japan's MS&AD group, per MSIG
Writes engineering insurance, per its own company profile
Business products checked have Product Disclosure Sheets in English and Malay
cons: No Contractors' All Risks page found on its current website
No published premium rates for commercial cover
CAR wording and extensions not available online; ask an agent or broker
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no published premium rates.
vendors.my_specific_note: Licensed under Malaysia's Financial Services Act 2013 and regulated by Bank Negara Malaysia; its site links PIDM's TIPS brochure. MSIG's earlier Contractors' All Risks page (under 'Other Commercial Insurance') now returns an error, so confirm the product with an agent or broker.

vendors.name: Zurich General Malaysia
vendors.tagline: Zurich's Malaysian general insurer, with CAR/EAR cover and Takaful versions
vendors.market_position: Zurich General Insurance Malaysia Berhad is part of the global Zurich Insurance Group, and Zurich Malaysia says its companies have branches in 30 locations nationwide. Its Contractors' All Risks / Erection All Risks policy covers civil works (CAR) or mechanical and electrical works (EAR). Sister company Zurich General Takaful Malaysia Berhad sells Contractor All Risks Takaful and Erection All Risks Takaful.
pros: One product covers civil works (CAR) or mechanical and electrical works (EAR)
Shariah-compliant Takaful versions from a sister company
Extensions include SRCC, inland transit, express freight, cross liability and extended maintenance
Product Disclosure Sheet and policy wording published on its website
cons: No published premium rates; quote by enquiry form, branch or phone
Conventional and Takaful versions are separate products from separate companies
Bank Negara fined the insurer RM1,040,000 in January 2026 for sanctions-screening breaches
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no published premium rates.
vendors.my_specific_note: Contractors can choose a conventional policy (Zurich General Insurance Malaysia Berhad) or Takaful cover (Zurich General Takaful Malaysia Berhad). Zurich says CAR/EAR benefits are protected by PIDM up to limits.

vendors.name: Tokio Marine Malaysia
vendors.tagline: Tokio Marine group's Malaysian general insurer, with a combined CAR/EAR product
vendors.market_position: Tokio Marine Insurans (Malaysia) Berhad is a general insurer in Japan's Tokio Marine group and a member of the General Insurance Association of Malaysia (PIAM). Its website carries a combined Contractors' All Risks / Erection All Risks product page. In May 2026 Bank Negara Malaysia allowed RHB Bank to start talks on selling RHB Insurance to Tokio Marine for integration with its Malaysian business, per The Star and The Edge.
pros: Combined Contractors' All Risks / Erection All Risks product
Part of Japan's Tokio Marine group
Member of the General Insurance Association of Malaysia (PIAM)
cons: No public premium rates found; quote-based
Ownership structure may change: merger talks with RHB Insurance began in May 2026
Ask for the Product Disclosure Sheet: policy details were not readable on its website
vendors.typical_pricing: Quote-based; no public premium rates found.
vendors.my_specific_note: Bank Negara Malaysia allowed RHB Bank in May 2026 to start talks on selling RHB Insurance to Tokio Marine for integration with Tokio Marine's Malaysian business; the two groups had held earlier talks in 2019. No completed deal was reported by the end of September 2026.

vendors.name: SQL Payroll
vendors.tagline: Malaysian payroll software on LHDN's MTD-compliant list, with EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB and HRDF
vendors.market_position: SQL Payroll is made by E Stream, the Shah Alam developer of SQL Account, and is sold as a cloud subscription or a permanent desktop licence. It calculates EPF, SOCSO, EIS, HRDF and PCB, produces the statutory forms and creates bank giro files for more than 25 Malaysian banks. LHDN's list of payroll software that meets its MTD calculation specifications (as at 29 September 2026) includes SQL Payroll, effective 19 July 2012.
pros: On LHDN's list of payroll software meeting its MTD calculation specifications
Published cloud prices from RM69 a month per company
Produces EPF Borang A, SOCSO Borang 2/3/8A, EA, CP39, CP22 and CP8D/Borang E
Bank giro payment files for more than 25 Malaysian banks
Works with SQL Account, with eLeave and eClaim modules
cons: Cloud price tiers cap active staff at 20 or 50
Extra users cost RM59 each; billing period not stated
Permanent desktop licence price not published
vendors.typical_pricing: SQL Payroll Cloud: RM69 a month per company for up to 20 active staff, RM79 a month for up to 50, plus RM59 per additional user; includes one year of phone support and updates. HRMS add-on RM49 a month per company. Permanent desktop licence is a one-time purchase, price not published. SST treatment not stated.
vendors.my_specific_note: Covers Malaysian statutory deductions (EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB, HRDF) and forms, with MyKad reader support. LHDN says employers using software on its MTD list need not obtain further verification of their tax-deduction calculations.

vendors.name: AutoCount HRMS (formerly AutoCount Cloud Payroll)
vendors.tagline: AutoCount's cloud payroll and HR suite (now branded AutoCount HRMS) for Malaysian employers
vendors.market_position: AutoCount HRMS, sold by some dealers as AutoCount Cloud Payroll, is the cloud payroll and HR product of Auto Count Sdn Bhd of Petaling Jaya, which has developed accounting software since 1996. Its group holding company, Autocount Dotcom Berhad, listed on Bursa Malaysia in May 2023 and, news reports say, moved to the Main Market on 25 February 2026. AutoCount says it has about 300 authorised dealers and that more than 190,000 employees have used AutoCount HRMS since its May 2019 launch.
pros: Free mode for payroll up to 3 employees (eLeave, eClaim, eAttendance up to 10)
Published plan prices
Covers EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB, Zakat and EA forms, AutoCount says
On LHDN's list of MTD-compliant payroll software providers
Sold and supported through about 300 authorised dealers
cons: Premium plan starts at 5 headcount
Express plan is payroll only, billed yearly from 30 headcount
Prices exclude SST and, on dealer pages, implementation
Buyers may deal with a dealer rather than AutoCount directly
vendors.typical_pricing: Free mode for payroll up to 3 employees; Premium from RM44/month (from 5 headcount, monthly or yearly, with eLeave, eClaim and eAttendance); Express from RM720/year (payroll only, from 30 headcount); Accountant from RM840/year (from 300 headcount). Prices exclude SST.
vendors.my_specific_note: AutoCount says the system complies with LHDN, KWSP (EPF), SOCSO and EIS requirements and covers income tax (PCB), Zakat, Tabung Haji and ASN deductions and EA forms. Auto Count Sdn Bhd is on LHDN's list of payroll software providers whose computerised PCB (MTD) calculation meets LHDN's specification (effective 24 June 2014), so employers using it need no separate LHDN verification. Its plan table lists payroll posting to cloud accounting, which suits a contractor already keeping its books in AutoCount Cloud Accounting.

vendors.name: Talenox
vendors.tagline: Cloud payroll, leave and claims for employers in Malaysia, Singapore and Hong Kong
vendors.market_position: Talenox is a cloud HR and payroll service run by Singapore-based Talenox Pte Ltd, with Malaysia, Singapore and Hong Kong editions. It sells self-serve plans online with published per-employee prices and a 30-day trial. Talenox says it is 'trusted by thousands of happy users'.
pros: Published per-employee prices and a 30-day Suite trial
EPF, SOCSO, EIS, PCB, Borang EA and Borang E, Talenox says
On LHDN's list of MTD-compliant payroll software providers
Same service covers Singapore and Hong Kong staff
Cancel any time; data stays viewable and exportable after a plan ends, Talenox says
cons: No free plan, only a 30-day trial
Minimum charge covers 5 employees
Cost rises with every active employee
Current low prices are a limited-time annual-plan offer
vendors.typical_pricing: Annual plans (limited-time offer, shown per month): Payroll or Leave RM3 per employee/month (normally RM5), from RM15/month for the first 5 employees; Suite (payroll, leave and claims) RM5 per employee/month (normally RM7), from RM25/month for the first 5. Monthly billing costs more; Talenox says annual billing saves about 15%.
vendors.my_specific_note: Talenox says it calculates EPF, SOCSO, EIS and PCB automatically, produces Borang EA and Borang E, supports HRDF and exports bank files for salary payment. Talenox Sdn Bhd is on LHDN's list of payroll software providers whose computerised PCB (MTD) calculation meets LHDN's specification (effective 20 December 2019). It suits a contractor with staff in Malaysia and also in Singapore or Hong Kong.

vendors.name: Kakitangan.com
vendors.tagline: Malaysian cloud payroll, leave, claims and attendance for small and growing employers
vendors.market_position: Kakitangan.com is a Malaysian cloud HR and payroll service run by Coastal Hectare Sdn Bhd of Kuala Lumpur, which says it is trusted by thousands of Malaysian businesses. News reports record a pitchIN equity crowdfunding round in 2016 and Series A funding from OSK Ventures International in January 2022. It sells payroll, leave, claims and attendance modules priced by employee count.
pros: EPF, SOCSO, EIS and PCB in every payslip, Kakitangan says
Automatic EA Form and Form E
On LHDN's list of MTD-compliant payroll software providers
Payroll, leave, claims and attendance in one platform
Accounting integration, including Xero
cons: No fixed prices in page text; cost comes from an online calculator
Larger organisations must ask sales for enterprise pricing
HRDF levy handling not mentioned on the payroll page
FAQ refers to 1-year subscription periods
vendors.typical_pricing: Priced by employee count through a calculator on Kakitangan's pricing page (3 to 400+ employees), with optional add-ons; no fixed figures could be read in this check. Enterprise pricing from sales.
vendors.my_specific_note: Kakitangan.com says it automates EPF, SOCSO, EIS and PCB deductions and generates the EA Form and Form E automatically. Coastal Hectare Sdn Bhd (Kakitangan.com) is on LHDN's list of payroll software providers whose computerised PCB (MTD) calculation meets LHDN's specification (effective 3 November 2017).

vendors.name: BrioHR
vendors.tagline: Malaysian modular HR suite, from recruitment and onboarding to payroll
vendors.market_position: BrioHR is a modular cloud HR suite from BrioHR Sdn Bhd of Kuala Lumpur, which says it has operated since 2018 and serves over 1,000 organisations. News reports in May 2025 said it raised a US$6.5 million Series A to expand in ASEAN. Payroll and the payroll bundles are sold for Malaysia and Singapore only.
pros: Published module and bundle prices
Prepares EA, CP39, Form E and CP8D, BrioHR says
Covers the HRDC levy as well as EPF, SOCSO, EIS and PCB
On LHDN's list of MTD-compliant payroll software providers
Recruitment, onboarding, attendance and performance modules in the same suite
cons: Minimum charge of USD50/month
Prices shown in USD rather than ringgit
Recruitment and onboarding modules start at USD120/month
A broad suite is more than a payroll-only buyer needs
vendors.typical_pricing: Payroll module from USD3/month (Malaysia and Singapore only); Payroll Essentials bundle from USD3.9/month, Payroll Pro from USD5/month, All-In-One from USD12/month. Billed on billable employees with a minimum of USD50/month.
vendors.my_specific_note: BrioHR says it calculates EPF, SOCSO, EIS, HRDC levy and PCB automatically and prepares EA, PCB2(II), CP39, Form E and CP8D, plus bank files. BrioHR Sdn Bhd is on LHDN's list of payroll software providers whose computerised PCB (MTD) calculation meets LHDN's specification (effective 17 February 2020).

vendors.name: CIDB Malaysia
vendors.tagline: Mandatory contractor registration and Green Card for construction personnel under Act 520
vendors.market_position: The Construction Industry Development Board (CIDB, or LPIPM) registers contractors under the Construction Industry Development Board Act 1994 (Act 520). Contractors apply through the CIMS portal and receive a PPK registration certificate by grade (G1 to G7) and category, plus an SPKK certificate for government works. CIDB also registers construction personnel, who receive the Green Card.
pros: Registration lets a contractor tender for and carry out construction work legally
Grade sets the works limit, from RM200,000 (G1) to no limit (G7)
SPKK certificate opens government works, with no extra registration fee
Green Card holders get takaful benefits, CIDB says
cons: Working unregistered risks a fine of RM10,000 to RM100,000
Registration must be renewed (1-3 years depending on CCD points)
Every site worker, supervisor and project manager needs a Green Card
Unpaid registration fees void an approval after 14 days
vendors.typical_pricing: PPK registration fee per year: G1 RM20, G2 RM80, G3 RM150, G4 RM350, G5 RM700, G6 RM1,000, G7 RM1,400, plus a RM50 processing fee per new application (RM30 for renewals); renewal at the same grade costs 50% of the registration fee; SPKK has no registration fee. Green Card: RM35 for 1 year up to RM135 for 5 years.
vendors.my_specific_note: Section 25 of Act 520 requires every local and foreign contractor to register with CIDB, and Section 29 sets a fine of RM10,000 to RM100,000 for breaches. Under Section 33(1) construction workers, site supervisors and project managers must also be registered (Green Card), which needs a safety induction course (SICW or eSICW). The registration number must be shown on the signboard at each site.

vendors.name: Board of Engineers Malaysia (BEM)
vendors.tagline: Statutory board that registers engineers and engineering consultancy practices under Act 138
vendors.market_position: The Board of Engineers Malaysia (BEM) is the board established by section 3 of the Registration of Engineers Act 1967 (Act 138), in force since 23 August 1972. It keeps the register of engineers and of engineering consultancy practices and runs professional examinations, including the Professional Competency Examination (PCE). BusinessToday Malaysia reported in August 2026 that amendments to the Act were expected to reach Parliament in its next session.
pros: Registration is the legal basis for providing professional engineering services
Only registered Professional Engineers may use the title 'Ir.'
A firm can register as an engineering consultancy practice and charge for engineering work
Registered engineers and practices can submit plans and designs to authorities
cons: Unregistered practice is an offence under the Act
Professional Engineer status needs Board-prescribed experience and an assessment
Registered engineers are subject to the Board's conditions and disciplinary powers
Further amendments to the Act are pending, news reports say
vendors.typical_pricing: Official fees are set by BEM and published on its website, which could not be read in this check.
vendors.my_specific_note: Under Act 138 only a registered Professional Engineer or a registered engineering consultancy practice may submit engineering plans, drawings and designs to an authority, and only a Professional Engineer may use the title 'Ir.'. A contractor whose job needs engineering submissions must therefore use a BEM-registered engineer or practice. The Act has been amended since its 2006 reprint, so check BEM's current categories before relying on a sign-off.

vendors.name: SSM (Companies Commission of Malaysia)
vendors.tagline: Registration of businesses, companies and LLPs in Malaysia
vendors.market_position: Suruhanjaya Syarikat Malaysia (SSM, the Companies Commission of Malaysia) sits under the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Cost of Living and administers the Companies Act 2016, the Registration of Businesses Act 1956 and the Limited Liability Partnerships Act 2012. Sole proprietorships and partnerships register through ezBiz, companies incorporate through MyCoID and LLPs register through MyLLP; companies file annual returns and financial statements through MBRS.
pros: Sets up the legal entity: sole proprietorship, partnership, company or LLP
Business registration costs RM30 or RM60 a year
Online registration through ezBiz, MyCoID and MyLLP
Company incorporation is a one-off RM1,000 fee
cons: Business registrations must be renewed, with fees charged per year
Private companies lodge an annual return (RM150) and financial statements
Name reservation for a company costs RM50 per 30 days
A company limited by guarantee costs RM3,000 to incorporate
vendors.typical_pricing: Business registration or renewal: RM30 per year (personal name) or RM60 per year (trade name), plus RM5 per branch per year. Company limited by shares (Sdn Bhd): RM1,000 to incorporate, RM50 per 30 days for name reservation, RM150 per annual return. Company limited by guarantee: RM3,000.
vendors.my_specific_note: A contractor first sets up its legal form with SSM: a sole proprietorship or partnership under the Registration of Businesses Act, or a Sdn Bhd under the Companies Act. CIDB's rules refer to these registrations; for example, CIDB's facilities category (F) is open only to ROC-registered companies (Sdn Bhd or Bhd) and certain other bodies at grade G4 and above.

vendors.name: LHDN / IRBM (Inland Revenue Board)
vendors.tagline: Income tax registration, the MyTax portal, employer PCB duties and MyInvois e-invoicing
vendors.market_position: The Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia (LHDN, IRBM or HASiL) is the country's direct tax administrator under the Income Tax Act 1967. It runs the MyTax portal, including e-Daftar for tax registration, handles employers' monthly tax deduction (PCB/MTD) rules and runs MyInvois, the national e-invoicing system rolled out in phases by turnover from August 2024.
pros: TIN registration online through e-Daftar on MyTax
Companies incorporated through MyCoID receive a TIN automatically
Businesses under RM3 million turnover are exempt from e-invoicing, subject to group rules
Interim relaxation until 31 December 2027 for the up-to-RM5 million phase
LHDN publishes a list of payroll software whose PCB calculation meets its specification
cons: Group, shareholder and related-company turnover can remove the RM3 million exemption
e-Invoice non-compliance can lead to prosecution under Section 120 of the Income Tax Act 1967
Employers carry monthly PCB/MTD duties as well as annual filing
e-Invoice rules change often (Guideline 4.8 and Specific Guideline 4.9 were issued in August-September 2026)
vendors.typical_pricing: LHDN's TIN registration page lists no registration fee. Tax, deductions and any penalties follow the Income Tax Act 1967.
vendors.my_specific_note: A company registers for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) through e-Daftar on MyTax (automatic for companies incorporated through SSM's MyCoID). Businesses with annual turnover up to RM5 million entered e-invoicing on 1 January 2026, but under LHDN's e-Invoice Guideline (version 4.8, 30 August 2026) those below RM3 million are exempt unless a shareholder company, holding company, related company or joint venture has turnover of RM3 million or more. For the up-to-RM5 million phase an interim relaxation runs until 31 December 2027, allowing consolidated e-invoices and no Section 120 prosecution for taxpayers who meet its conditions. See our MyInvois guide for the construction specifics.

vendors.name: EPF / KWSP
vendors.tagline: Mandatory employer registration and monthly retirement-savings contributions
vendors.market_position: The Employees Provident Fund (EPF, or KWSP) is the statutory retirement-savings fund under the Employees Provident Fund Act 1991. Employers must register with the EPF and pay monthly contributions, covering both the employer and employee shares, for their employees. News reports say contributions became mandatory for non-Malaysian employees from October 2025 wages, at 2% each from employer and employee.
pros: Registering lets an employer hire and pay staff in line with the EPF Act
Contributions build employees' retirement savings in the Fund
Employer and employee may choose to contribute above the statutory rate (s.43(3))
cons: Registration is due within the first week of the first month wages are paid
Contributions are due every month for every covered employee
Failing to register or pay can bring a fine of up to RM10,000 or imprisonment
Wage records must be kept for at least six years
vendors.typical_pricing: Employers pay monthly contributions (employer and employee shares) at the statutory rates set under the EPF Act 1991. Current rates are published by the EPF, whose website could not be read in this check.
vendors.my_specific_note: Under section 41 of the EPF Act 1991 an employer must register with the EPF before the end of the first week of the first month in which it pays wages that attract contributions, and must then pay contributions every month. The 2006 reprint of the Act sets up to three years' imprisonment or a fine of up to RM10,000 for failing to register or to pay. Contractors with foreign workers should check the current rules for non-Malaysian employees, which the Cabinet was reviewing in July 2026, news reports say.

vendors.name: SOCSO / PERKESO
vendors.tagline: Mandatory social security (SOCSO) and Employment Insurance (EIS) registration for employers
vendors.market_position: PERKESO (the Social Security Organisation, SOCSO) runs the Employment Injury and Invalidity schemes under the Employees' Social Security Act 1969 and the Employment Insurance System (EIS) under the Employment Insurance System Act 2017. Every employer with one or more employees must register and pay contributions, which it does online through the ASSIST portal. News reports say foreign workers were brought under SOCSO from January 2019 and under the Invalidity Scheme in 2024.
pros: Employment injury, invalidity and job-loss (EIS) cover for employees
Registration and payment online through ASSIST, with payment also by the PRIHATIN app
Foreign workers are covered under the Employment Injury and Invalidity schemes, news reports say
Several payment channels, including FPX, direct debit and bank counters
cons: Contributions due by the 15th of each month; late payment carries 6% a year interest
Work accidents must be reported within 48 hours
Non-payment can bring up to two years' imprisonment or a RM10,000 fine (2006 text of the Act)
Statutory scheme: covered employers cannot opt out
vendors.typical_pricing: No registration fee is stated on PERKESO's registration page. Contributions follow the statutory rate tables under Act 4 and Act 800, on wages up to RM6,000 a month since 1 October 2024; LINDUNG 24 Jam adds an employee-paid 0.75% of wages in its first two years.
vendors.my_specific_note: Employers register themselves and their workers (Borang 1 and 2, with a separate form for foreign workers) through ASSIST, pay contributions by the 15th of the following month and must report work accidents within 48 hours. Since 1 October 2024 contributions are calculated on wages up to RM6,000 a month. The newer LINDUNG 24 Jam scheme for accidents outside working hours is paid by employees, optional for Malaysians and mandatory for foreign workers, PERKESO says. The CIDB Green Card's takaful benefits are separate from SOCSO cover.

vendors.name: HRD Corp
vendors.tagline: Training-levy registration for employers under the PSMB Act 2001
vendors.market_position: HRD Corp (Pembangunan Sumber Manusia Berhad) collects the human resources development levy under the Pembangunan Sumber Manusia Berhad Act 2001 and uses it to fund training for registered employers. The Act's coverage was extended to further industries from 1 March 2021. The minister said in August 2025 that over 100,000 employers and 4.8 million employees were registered, NST reported.
pros: The levy can fund training for the employer's own staff
Registered employers can use 'HRD Corp claimable' training programmes
HRD Corp approved RM2.62 billion of financial assistance in 2025, NST reported
cons: Registration is compulsory at 10 or more employees in covered industries
The levy is a monthly cost based on wages
Management changed in 2026 after PAC and MACC findings, news reports say
vendors.typical_pricing: Levy rates are set under the PSMB Act 2001 and published by HRD Corp; its website could not be read in this check, so no rate is stated here.
vendors.my_specific_note: Employers with 10 or more employees in a covered industry must register with HRD Corp and pay the monthly levy, which registered employers can then draw on for training. Since the March 2021 expansion covered further industries, a growing contractor should check whether it has passed the threshold. In September 2026 the High Court dismissed a Malaysian Bar challenge to the levy, NST reported.
